text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- The Yugoslav government will insist on comprehensive reforms aimed at building a market economy harmonised with the EU, said new Deputy Prime Minister Danko Djunic.
- Yugoslav parliamentary delegation leaves for Seoul to take part in the 97th Interparliamentary Union conference.
- Over 99 percent of Eastern Slavonia Serbs opt in a referendum for a single region. The Serb regional parliament will decide Tuesday if Serbs will participate in the upcoming local elections.
- Albanian unrests resulted in increase of prices of bananas and citrus fruit on the Yugoslav market.
- Serbian government proposes deferrment of farmers' tax payments to August 15.
- The Serbian capital assessment Agency will become part of the ownership transformation ministry and will be renamed Directorate when the new ownership transformation law enters into effect.
- Talks on Kosovo are necessary but should be conducted in the country, says spokeseman of the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia Ivica Dacic.
- The Yugoslav-Kosovo Albanian talks in New York should open the door to Serb-Albanian dialogue, said leader of opposition Serbian Renewal Movement Vuk Draskovic at the beginning of the round table.
NASA BORBA
- Belgrade university deans warn about alarming financial situation at the university, call on the government to pay its outstanding debt of 32 million dinars.
- Belgrade mayor Zoran Djindjic to meet Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic and discuss repayment of Serbia's debt to the city.
- The slight consoldiation of the dinar on the black market exchange rate is unfavourable for exporters, say businessmen.
- Nineteen Belgrade schools to stage a one-day warning strike protesting over government failure to fulfill its promise and pay out teachers' wages regularly.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Ukrainian plane landed at Belgrade Surcin airport late Monday night carrying bodies of Yugoslav mercenaries who fought in the civil war in Zaire. All mercenaries from Yugoslavia and Bosnian Serb republic expected to return shortly because their contract has expired.
- Montenegrin official independent trade union federation schedules protest rally in Podgorica on May 1 over deteriorating social position of workers. It staged similar rally last year.
- Yugoslavia's central bank neglects small banks even though they can be a door to foreign capital coming to our country, says founder of small Control bank Momcilo Filipovic.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Yugoslav Crown Prince Aleksandar criticises Serbian patriarch Pavle in an open letter.
- Mercedes to extend credit to Belgrade city transport for purchase of buses.
BORBA
- Chinese-Polish vessel arrived in Montenegro's port of Bar marking the beginning of a regular shipping line from Bar to Chinese ports.
- Serbian agriculture machine factory Zmaj to complete 200 combines by May for markets in China and 150 for the domestic market by end of June.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA

- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic and Prime Minister Milo Djukanovice receive in seperate meetings Italian Ambassador to Yugoslavia Francesco Buscone and Italian consul in Montenegro Stephano Mistreta.
- Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic to visit Slovakia at the invitation of Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar.
- Lack of funds put in question planned reconstruction of the Podgorica-Trebjesnica section of the Belgrade-Bar railway.

- Out of 130 million dinars earmarked for public works in Montenegro 27 percent will be invested in roads, said Miodrag Raicevic director of Directorate for public works of Montenegro. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 2224254
